A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix B report original benchmarking experiments on 26 binary-classification datasets, including AUBCs, rankings, and model-compatibility analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results and reports additional model-compatibility results in Section 5.1 and Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: The pool-based active-learning framework and US-C/US-NC procedures are retained. Expanded strategy descriptions and the revised framework diagram clarify existing procedures without introducing a new proposed algorithm, objective, or architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 26 binary-classification datasets. Additional compatibility plots use datasets already benchmarked in v1. Other domains and tasks appear only in related-work and future-work discussion.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains the same 17 query strategies, Uniform, and BSO. Table 6 narrows the original-benchmark-setting comparison to Google Uniform by removing the libact and ALiPy entries there, while retaining those implementations under the other settings.

E3.justification: Table 4 revises the reported ALBL configuration from LR(C=1) to a combination of US-C, US-NC, and HintSVM with shared H. This changes a previously stated setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. The data split, initial labeled-pool size, and query budget are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B.2 substantially extend the compatibility analysis: the LR/SVM/RF model-pair grids now cover all 26 datasets rather than 10. Results are grouped by the best compatible model, with explicit examination of four cases favoring incompatible models.

E5.justification: Section 3 clarifies that the retained 100/10 runs are the first successfully completed experiments from 150/15 attempts, skipping failures. This refines run-selection reporting; the run counts, standard-deviation reporting, confidence-interval construction, and statistical-test procedures remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds model-pair results for 16 datasets and the aggregate finding that compatible pairs perform best on 22 of 26 datasets. Section 5.2 newly states that all Friedman p-values are below 0.05. Main Tables 1 and 3 and Figure 5's counts are unchanged; Table 6 removes the original-setting results 0.7570 for libact and 0.7502 for ALiPy.

T1.justification: The pool-update equations, AUBC-difference and applicability definitions, BMDR/SPAL mathematics, and Appendix D's eigenvalue-shift argument are retained. The added explanation of model compatibility clarifies the existing distinction between query-oriented and task-oriented models.

C1.justification: The abstract and three central contributions retain their meaning: reproducible benchmarking, model compatibility explaining discrepancies, competitive uncertainty sampling, and limited benefits of many strategies over Uniform. The conclusion's explicit count of 10 elaborates the retained 'more than half' claim.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the compatibility recommendation with exceptions and conjectures that heterogeneous models can help by exploring more diverse examples. Sections 2–3 and the expanded Appendix E substantially develop applicability boundaries, excluded deep-learning methods, failure conditions, alternative evaluation considerations, and sensitivity to experimental settings.

D1.justification: Section 3 explicitly states the use of library-default strategy hyperparameters and clarifies failure handling. Table 4 revises ALBL configuration information, and Section 5.2 adds a precise notebook location for Friedman results. The listed hardware, solver fixes, and main repository links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 and Appendix E substantially broaden positioning through deep-active-learning methods and benchmarks, reproducibility literature, and applications beyond binary classification. Additions include BADGE, WAAL, and work by Munjal and Lüth. New Appendix A.6 and Table 7 explicitly compare the benchmark with its predecessors.

P1.justification: Section 2.1 is extensively rewritten into a four-category strategy overview, and Section 3 is reorganized to foreground the study's settings. Compatibility explanations and Appendix E are substantially rewritten and expanded, alongside editing throughout the paper, although the main section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, swaps Figure 5's panels and adds numerical labels, introduces comparison Tables 7–8, and expands and regroups compatibility plots into Figures 7–12. Captions are expanded. The existing applicability scatterplot is retained as Figure 6, previously Figure 8.

improvement.justification: Broader compatibility evidence and explicit exceptions make the central recommendation better supported and qualified, while expanded background and scope discussion improve clarity. These are incremental gains over v1's existing benchmark. New reporting inconsistencies temper the benefit: Table 7 lists 35 binary datasets for Zhan et al., conflicting with 26 in Appendix A.1, and Section 5.3's new 'less than 16' statement conflicts with Figure 5.
